reason: The agent misinterpreted “Draft a new” as requiring an inactive draft. It saved the catalog price rule with Active set to No and did not apply it, so the rule would not offer the requested discount. It needed to create the site-wide 20% rule for all customer groups with Active enabled and save/apply it.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “Draft a new” as requiring draft/inactive status and explicitly turned Active off. The saved Spring Sale rule was therefore Inactive and did not actually offer the 20% site-wide discount. It needed to leave the rule Active while applying the 20% percentage discount to the website and all customer groups.

The agent misinterpreted “Draft a new” as requiring draft/inactive status and deliberately left the rule disabled. The requested rule needed to offer the discount, so it should have been created as Active (with the specified site-wide scope, all customer groups, and 20% percentage discount), rather than saved as an inactive rule.

The agent misread “Draft a new marketing price rule” as requiring an inactive draft. It left Active set to No and saved without applying, so the 20% site-wide promotion was not enabled. It needed to create the rule with Active set to Yes (and save/apply it as required) for the selected website and all customer groups.

The agent created a Cart Price Rule, but a site-wide marketing price rule for all products/customers should have been created under Marketing → Catalog Price Rule. It also used the embellished name “Spring Sale 20% Off Sitewide” rather than the requested Spring Sale name. It needed to save an inactive Catalog Price Rule named Spring Sale, scoped to all websites and customer groups, with a 20% percentage discount and no product conditions.

The agent created a Cart Price Rule, but a site-wide marketing price discount should have been created under Marketing → Catalog Price Rule. It needed to configure a new catalog rule for “Spring Sale,” select the website and all customer groups, leave product conditions blank for all products, and set the action to a 20% discount. The agent also assumed “draft” meant inactive without explicit support.

The agent created another rule named “Spring Sale” even though an inactive Spring Sale rule already existed (ID 3). This left duplicate matching records, so the grader could resolve the name to the pre-existing rule rather than the newly configured ID 5 and find incorrect attributes. It needed to inspect the existing Spring Sale draft and update/verify that record, or otherwise avoid creating an ambiguous duplicate.

The rule was saved with the name “Spring Sale” instead of the requested exact name “spring sale.” The grader likely performs an exact field match; the agent needed to preserve the task’s lowercase rule name while keeping the inactive 20% site-wide configuration.

It needed to leave/save the rule as inactive (and, given the existing matching draft, update that entry rather than create an active duplicate) while setting the $10 whole-cart discount for all customer groups.

The agent saved the new rule as Active because it left the default “Active: Yes” setting enabled. Since the task asked to draft the rule, it needed to set the rule inactive before saving, while retaining the $10 fixed whole-cart discount and all customer groups.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft a new rule” as requiring an inactive Magento rule and explicitly set Active to No. An inactive rule cannot offer the requested $10 checkout discount. It needed to save the new Fall Discount rule as Active while retaining the whole-cart fixed $10 action, no coupon, and all customer groups.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “draft” as requiring an inactive rule and switched Active to No. As saved, the rule cannot offer the $10 checkout discount to customers. It needed to leave the new Fall Discount rule active while applying a $10 fixed amount discount for the whole cart to all customer groups.

The agent saved the rule as Active because it left the default “Active: Yes” enabled. A rule described as a draft needed to be inactive/disabled before saving. It also created a duplicate “Fall Discount” instead of addressing the existing inactive rule, which could cause the grader to inspect the unchanged record.

The agent misinterpreted “Draft a new…” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly switched Active to No. The requested sale rule needed to be created with the configured $15 whole-cart checkout discount for all customer groups while remaining active; saving it as Inactive caused the grader mismatch.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “Draft a new” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly turned Active to No. “Draft” was the creation instruction, not a requested status; the sale rule needed to be saved as active so it would offer the $15 whole-cart checkout discount to all customer groups.

The agent incorrectly interpreted “Draft a new” as requiring an inactive rule and explicitly turned Active off. As saved, the rule cannot offer the $15 checkout discount. It needed to leave the new cart price rule active while selecting all customer groups and applying a $15 fixed amount discount for the whole cart.

The agent created a second duplicate “Mother's day sale” rule even though an inactive rule with that exact name already existed (ID 6). This left the original matching record unconfigured, so a grader resolving the rule by name could inspect the wrong record. It needed to edit the existing matching draft—or otherwise ensure there was only one uniquely identifiable rule—with all customer groups and a $15 whole-cart fixed discount.

The agent saved the new rule as Active even though the task asked to draft it. It needed to disable the Active toggle before saving so the new Mother's day sale rule remained inactive/draft while retaining the $15 whole-cart discount and all customer groups.

The rule was saved as Active because the agent left the default “Active” checkbox enabled. Since the task requested a draft rule, it needed to set Active to No/inactive before saving; the other core settings ($15 fixed amount for the whole cart and all customer groups) were configured correctly.

The agent correctly navigated to Reports → Sales → Orders and deliberately set the report’s inclusive date range to 1/1/2022 through 12/31/2022, accurately deriving “last year” from the supplied date of 3/15/2023. The successful state was reached through targeted, grounded UI actions rather than guessing.
